text: You're a new ServiceNow admin on your first day, and your manager asks for three things before stand-up: open the Incident table's list view, narrow it to incidents assigned to the Network group, and confirm your own time zone is set correctly. Let's walk through it, step by step, entirely in words.

Skip the Application Navigator's tree entirely. Click into the filter box at the top of the left-side panel, type "incident.list," and press Enter. That opens the incident table's list view immediately — every record you have permission to see, with no module and no pre-applied filter standing in the way.

Above the column headers sits a breadcrumb and a filter icon shaped like a funnel. Click it to open the condition builder. Set the field to Assignment group, the operator to "is," and the value to Network, then click Run. The list refreshes to show only incidents routed to that group, and the record count updates to match — and you could save this exact view to Favorites if you'll need it again tomorrow.

Those timestamps on the list you just filtered display according to your own personal time zone preference, not any system-wide setting. Click your profile picture in the top-right corner of the header, open your profile or preferences, and check the time zone field. If it's wrong, fix it right there — never in System Properties, because this setting belongs to you alone, not the whole instance.

Shortcut, filter, correct scope — that's the exact sequence that separates someone who's merely seen ServiceNow from someone who can actually move around it under pressure on day one. Next up, Chapter Three: what a table actually is in ServiceNow.
